authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan surveys. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have 8 hours, i will review once your time is done.

proposals.evidence: Zoller explicitly derives Indus Kohistani həlīẓ/həlīṣ turmeric from haridrā (CDIAL 13992); Turner also gives Shina haliẓi. The survey hāliź/hæliṣ forms preserve this diagnostic northwestern outcome, including the source’s palatal/retroflex notation and final vowel where present. This is not the unrelated halīṣā plough-pole entry printed immediately above in Zoller.

proposals.evidence: Zoller explicitly compares Indus Kohistani huigi/hugi garlic to Pashto hūga. These closely matching survey forms are assigned as loans using the existing Pashto ūgā donor attestation; that node represents the Pashto lexical family, not a claim that the exact Charsadda vowel/initial realization was the local donor. Transmission through a neighbouring Kohistani variety remains possible.
